verdict.rationale: Lambda's On-Demand Cloud offers self-serve GPU VMs that can be launched from the console or programmatically through the Lambda Cloud API, which a runtime probe confirms is live. Instances come with Lambda Stack drivers and frameworks preinstalled and are reachable over SSH or JupyterLab, so code can run immediately, and a community user reports launching a GH200 and working in Jupyter. Missing for 10: independent measurement of the 'in minutes' time-to-running claim (it is vendor-stated only, with capacity on first-come access).

support.subject: As a developer, I can provision an on-demand GPU instance from the console or API and be running code on it within minutes

citations.quote: On-Demand Cloud (ODC) provides on-demand access to Linux-based, GPU-backed virtual machine instances.
You can also launch instances programmatically by using the Lambda Cloud API.
Deploy NVIDIA B200, H100, A100, or GH200 instances in minutes with self-serve, first-come access.
Lambda also preinstalls Lambda Stack, a standard set of AI/ML-related drivers, tools, and frameworks, on the instance
You can connect to your On-Demand Cloud (ODC) instances directly through SSH or by using the preinstalled JupyterLab server.
the instance-provisioning REST API is live and key-gated
